definition: Vera Demberg (born 1981) is a German computational linguist and professor of computer science and computational linguistics at Saarland University.
details: Her research interests include cognitive models of human language comprehension, natural language generation, experimental psycholinguistics, multimodal language processing in a dual-task setting, and experimental and computational discourse research and pragmatics.

explainer.lead: Vera Demberg is a Professor of Computer Science and Computational Linguistics. Her work spans computational linguistics and artificial intelligence.

contributions.name: From 2010 to 2016, Vera Demberg led an independent research group on cognitive models of human language processing and their application to speech dialog systems in the Cluster of Excellence “Multimodal Computing and Interaction” at the University of Saarland.
She has authored and co-authored numerous papers on the study of computational linguistics and natural language processing.

timeline.what: Vera Demberg studied computational linguistics at the Institute for Machine Language Processing at the University of Stuttgart from 2001 to 2006.
She then completed a Master's degree in Artificial Intelligence at the University of Edinburgh from 2004 to 2005.
She received her Ph.D. from the Department of Computer Science there from 2006 to 2010.
